text:
Olivia Chen: FYI saw a pretty clear p95 decode latency jump on the canary after yesterday's runtime merge. p95 went from ~120ms to ~320ms on chat-decode workloads. :eyes:
Raj Patel: Seen that too. Is this on all models or only long-seq ones?
Olivia Chen: Mostly long-seq (>=1024) paths, but some mid-seq cases got worse. Throughput looks similar, but tail latency and GPU kernel-switch counts are way up.
perf-bot: CI perf job failed: https://ci.example.com/builds/12345 - p95 regression detected (+170ms) on decode-bench.
Maya Gomez: I pulled a perf flame and a kernel-switch trace. Attn kernel handoffs spike right at token ~40 for cached KV sequences. Link: https://artifacts.example.com/flames/2109998888
Theo Li: I ran a quick profile on a repro VM. KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~12% after merge, and the kernel selector is choosing the 'long-seq' attention implementation much more often. Looks like the selector scoring logic changed.
Raj Patel: Can someone bisect the merge range? If it's a heuristic weight change that's easier to revert.
Olivia Chen: Starting git bisect on the release branch now. range: v1.14.2..main (merges from last 48h).
Raj Patel: Commands I used earlier:```
git bisect start HEAD v1.14.2
git bisect run ./tools/perf/run_decode_bench.sh --model=gpt-medium --seq=2048
```
Maya Gomez: I noticed a suspicious diff in PR #4821 (batcher/heuristics rewrite). Key line changed:```
- score += kernel_pref * 0.1;
+ score += kernel_pref * 10.0; // prefer long-seq kernel aggressively
```
Theo Li: That multiplication looks catastrophic. A x100 weight increase will swamp other signals and trigger kernel switching even when prefix cache is hot.
Olivia Chen: Bisect landed on commit 3f7c9b2 which is the PR merge of #4821. Confirmed by reproducer.
Raj Patel: Reproduced locally. If I revert that single change, p95 returns to ~125ms.
sre-bot: Rollout hold placed on canary for release-1.14.3 by @Olivia Chen — reason: p95 decode regression.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment paused.
Maya Gomez: Quick suggested fix: gate the aggressive weight behind an experiment flag and restore previous constant (0.1) while we investigate. Patch:```
- score += kernel_pref * 10.0;
+ if (feature_flags.get("batcher_kernel_experiment", false)) {
+   score += kernel_pref * 10.0;
+ } else {
+   score += kernel_pref * 0.1;
+ }
```
Raj Patel: I'm pushing a hotfix PR that reverts the weight change and adds an integration test to assert no >50ms p95 delta on decode-bench. Will link PR shortly.
Theo Li: Also adding a KV-cache regression unit test — the selector should prefer kernels that preserve KV layout when cache hits >80%.
Olivia Chen: Plan: (1) land hotfix revert PR + small test, (2) run perf CI with benchmark tag, (3) roll canary forward with new image if green, (4) follow-up deeper investigation to design a safe experiment (gradual ramp, A/B, metrics for kernel-switch counts).
Raj Patel: PR: https://git.example.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4880 - revert weight change + test.
perf-bot: Perf CI queued for PR 4880.
Maya Gomez: After revert on my local, KV hit-rate and kernel-switch counts are back to previous baseline.
sre-bot: Canary hold will remain until PR 4880 passes perf CI and is deployed to canary.
Olivia Chen: Thanks everyone. If you touch kernel selector/batcher heuristics this week please ping this thread and add a perf benchmark. We'll add a follow-up postmortem with root cause analysis and the decision matrix. :thumbsup:
Raj Patel: Filed follow-up issue: https://issues.example.com/INF-1029 - Investigate weight scale effects and add rollout safety for heuristic changes.
Theo Li: I'll own the postmortem write-up and include flame graphs + kv-hit timelines.
Olivia Chen: Closing loop when canary is green.
